reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation / GeneReviews
clinicalPearls: A rare, typically lethal neonatal genodermatosis defined by rigid, taut, thin skin that severely restricts movement
The tight skin causes a fixed facial expression, small pinched nose, open O-shaped mouth, micrognathia and multiple joint contractures
Pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory insufficiency from restricted chest movement are the usual cause of early death, often within days of birth
Most cases result from loss-of-function variants in ZMPSTE24, the enzyme that processes prelamin A into mature lamin A; some arise from LMNA variants
There is often a history of polyhydramnios, reduced fetal movements and premature birth
Skin may show erosions and a characteristic thin, tightly adherent epidermis on histology
Management is almost always palliative given the near-uniform lethality; genetic counselling is central for recurrence risk
reference.pathophysiology: Restrictive dermopathy is a laminopathy caused by failure of normal maturation of the nuclear lamina protein lamin A. Loss-of-function variants in ZMPSTE24, the zinc metalloprotease that cleaves the farnesylated prelamin A precursor, or certain LMNA variants, lead to accumulation of abnormal farnesylated prelamin A. This toxic precursor distorts nuclear architecture and impairs the function of skin and connective tissue cells, producing the rigid, hypoplastic dermis, taut skin, joint contractures and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia that characterise the lethal phenotype.
additionalInvestigations: Molecular testing of ZMPSTE24 and LMNA
Skin biopsy with histology showing a thin dermis and abnormal epidermis
Detailed dysmorphology examination and clinical photography
Placental and fetal assessment where a pregnancy history is available
Genetic counselling and consideration of prenatal testing in future pregnancies
redFlags: Progressive respiratory failure from pulmonary hypoplasia and restricted chest expansion
Severe feeding difficulty from restricted facial and oral movement
Skin erosions with risk of infection and fluid loss
Any presentation is inherently critical given the near-uniform neonatal lethality
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is extremely poor: restrictive dermopathy is almost always lethal in the neonatal period, usually from respiratory insufficiency, so care is generally palliative and directed at comfort and family support.
pitfalls: Mistaking the taut skin for a severe congenital ichthyosis such as harlequin ichthyosis
Pursuing aggressive intervention when the condition is near-uniformly lethal, rather than focusing on palliation
Overlooking the laminopathy basis and its implications for recurrence-risk counselling
Failing to arrange confirmatory genetics to guide future pregnancies
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Recognise the almost uniformly lethal neonatal course and centre care on palliation, comfort and family support rather than cure
Guide neonatal respiratory support decisions by the severe pulmonary hypoplasia, with careful goals-of-care discussion
Manage skin fragility and erosions with gentle emollients, meticulous wound care and infection prevention
Support feeding and provide analgesia given the restricted mouth, joint contractures and taut skin
Confirm the diagnosis with ZMPSTE24 and LMNA molecular testing
Offer genetic counselling and prenatal or preimplantation testing in future pregnancies given autosomal recessive inheritance
Involve neonatology, clinical genetics and palliative care in coordinated multidisciplinary support
